The avenue
Over the hearth: a painted boat with no lantern, nosing in toward a hill where every hand holds up what light it had. The grove's telling.
A star chart in gilt on deep blue. Small notes in the margin mark which stars ring truest through a tuning glass.
The forge is hot. Open your manufacture window to smith.
Aldith's copy desk: a fair copy of this spring's register lines, each one initialled twice, once by her and once by Hemmen.
Wynn's loom, strung with cape cloth in cobalt and cream. Mara sells what comes off it on the plaza; the hem stitch is her mother's.
The watch duty board: a sheet pinned up for each people that keeps the watch, the names in eight hands, and nobody's name at the top.
Jessamy's net frame: a boat's net hung from the mending pole, half its knots new. She says she can tell which harbour tied the old ones.
A notice under the palace's seal, the first to come down in living memory: a south gate and a north one, cut this year beside the two old west gates. It calls this a renovation.
The map table of Landfall: the isle painted under glass, every post of the eight peoples marked in its own colour. Nobody has marked the keep.
The Luminous seat. Hemmen will not sit in it: a clerk who votes is a record that decides.
The Votary seat. Ostrid will not leave her door, and no other Votary will sit in her place.
The Mycelari seat. Lichen has grown over its arms and round its foot; the Mycelari asked that nobody scrape it off, and nobody has.
The Stoneborn place. They sent no chair and no delegate, only a stone cut from their own quarry and stood where a chair would stand: a stone, they say, keeps a place well enough.
The register volume of the great freeze, open at six names in one shaking hand. Two of the six lines have never been closed.
A letter slot in the shut door at the top of the stair. Whatever goes through is gone by morning; in two hundred years, two things have come back down.
Bettany's recipe book, spine split. The first page is in her mother's hand: delta eel, slow over smoke. Under it, in Bettany's: never rush it.
A card propped on the desk, in a careful Votary hand: Calloway's lends nothing. Read anything in the back room for as long as the lamps last; what leaves the shop leaves it paid for.
A history of Landfall, copied out of the Landing Register's margins: who came ashore, who stayed, and which people garrisons which wall. The chapter on the palace runs to two lines.
New arrivals, chalked in two columns: manuals off the Westhaven boat, tomes copied fair in Mirrorhold, and a crate of craft books still to be counted. Ask at the desk.
Ennis's catalogue: every book in the shop, entered twice in two inks and checked against the shelves each evening. The two columns have agreed for nine years.
